# s380 — slicer goals prints '(none set)' and a Python list literal when only catalog goal records exist

**Findings:** ork interview 2026-10-18 (squalor-xyz/ork docs/review-2026-10-18.md) · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**Not in this slice:** the JSON shape of `goals`, or how `catalog list` prints records.

## Why

In a project with goal records but no goals prose, `slicer goals` prints this:

```
Goals:
  (none set)

['  C01  Ship it', '    Ship the thing.']
```

(Reproduced on a fresh `init` with `catalog add --kind goal` and `--kind non_goal`. Found in the ork repo, ork review 2026-10-18 finding 22.) `cmd_goals` (`src/slicer/cli.py`, near line 2990) interpolates the list from `_catalog_lines` straight into an f-string. It also prints `(none set)` whenever the prose is empty, even when records follow. The same list literal appears when there is prose and records. `test_Goals_IncludesGoalRecords_AndNotRequirements` (`tests/test_catalog.py`) only uses `assertIn`, so it passes on the broken output.

## Files

- `src/slicer/cli.py` (`cmd_goals`).
- `tests/test_goals.py`.
- `CHANGELOG.md` under Fixed.

## Failing tests

- `test_Goals_RecordsOnly_ListsRecordsWithoutNoneSet`: with records and no prose, the text is exactly `Goals:\n  C01  Ship it\n    Ship the thing.\n\nNon-goals:\n  C02  No cloud\n`, with no `(none set)` and no `[`.
- `test_Goals_ProseAndRecords_PrintsRecordLinesNotAList`: with prose and records, the record lines follow the prose after one blank line, one per line.
- `test_Goals_Unset_ReportsNoneSetInTextAndEmptyInJson` stays as it is: no prose and no records still prints `(none set)`.

## Implement

1. Write the tests; watch them go red.
2. Join the record lines with newlines, and print `(none set)` only when a block has neither prose nor records.
3. CHANGELOG entry under Fixed.
4. Mutation-check each new test.
